newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Degroof raises UM to market outperformer.
newsitem.headline: Degroof raises UM to market outperformer.

text.p: Belgium's Bank Degroof said on Thursday it upgraded its recommendation on shares in non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere (UM) from 'market performer' to 'market outperformer'.
"Union Minere is right now one of the most attractive industrial shares on the Brussels Stock Exchange," analyst Alexandre Schmitz said.
UM reported group net profit of 391 million francs for calendar 1996 against a loss of 954 million the previous year. It was the group's first profit since 1990.
"For the first time since the start of the 1990s, group management is displaying a cautious confidence in the turnaround of profitability for the coming years," Bank Degroof said in a research note.

"The appreciation of the dollar, the rise in the zinc price and the first signs of an improving economic climate should allow the group to benefit, as early as 1997, from strong growth in its net current earnings," Schmitz said.

UM was unlikely to feel any significant impact on results from a comprehensive industrial restructuring plan before 1998, analysts said. But Schmitz said that once the restructuring plan was completed UM could see impressive results.
By 1430 GMT Union Minere shares were up 1.67 percent at 2,740 francs.
Union Miniere is 50 percent owned by Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique.
